thread:
alex: Quick heads-up — I'm seeing a weird split between replay and synthetic runs after the kernel-routing change. Replay p95 ~38ms, synthetic p95 ~62ms on the same instance type. Anyone else seeing this?

jia: Yep, saw that too on the nightly. p99 looks closer, but tails differ. Could be batching behaviour + KV warmup. :thinking_face:

rachel: Do we have the exact microbatch config used for the synth test? I think loadgen used burst mode w/ batch_timeout=20ms. Replays preserve original inter-arrival, so batching patterns diverge.

alex: Good call. Here's the synth command I used:```
./loadgen --profile=large-chat --concurrency=200 --batch-timeout=20ms --microbatch=auto --kv-policy=none 
--kernel-prefer=fused_attention```
(the replay was just replay_tool --trace=prod-2026-03-01)

sam: The kernel selection heuristic can also flip depending on observed sequence length distribution. Fused kernels win at medium seq lengths but lose if microbatching pushes sequence-length-equivalent compute to another codepath. Replay keeps the exact seq distribution; synth might inflate short requests into larger batches.

perf-bot: Test 1835123468 completed: p95=61.8ms, p99=180.2ms, mean=28.4ms, KV_hit_rate=42% (synth)

jia: Also remember replay will preserve KV cache hit patterns — if we don't prewarm KV for synth, first-token latencies blow up and skew p95. We should instrument KV_hit_rate by prefix length.

rachel: Proposed experiment: 1) run synth with batch-timeout matched to replay median inter-arrival (use --batch-timeout-from-trace). 2) force kernel selection to the same path (e.g., --kernel-forced=fused_attention) 3) run replay with synthetic jitter to mimic bursts. Then compare p95 and p99.

alex: I can do 1+2 today. For 3, do we have a jitter generator? We tried simple poisson jitter last time but maybe need heavy-tailed bursts.

sam: Use loadgen's --burst-profile=on_off with Pareto on-time to emulate tailiness. Example:```
--burst-profile=on_off --on-pareto-alpha=1.5 --on-mean=100ms --off-mean=1s```
That exaggerates bursts and will surface batching convoys.

perf-bot: New run 1835123520 (synth, batch-timeout-from-trace, kernel-forced=fused_attention) finished: p95=40.2ms, p99=145.6ms, KV_hit_rate=79%

rachel: Nice — forcing kernel made a big difference when KV was warm. Suggest we add a small constant prewarm window for synth tests to stabilize KV. Also we should record per-token histograms (not just per-request) for p95/p99.

jia: Agree. Also proposal: use both metrics (SLO-targeted p95 on first-token for interactive flows, but look at p99 for tail accounting across entire request). Document tradeoffs: microbatch sizing reduces cost but can amplify tail if convoy forms.

alex: Action items: (1) I'll run the forced-kernel + burst-profile matrix across two instance types and post results. (2) @rachel please add KV prewarm flag to our synth harness. (3) @sam can you enumerate kernel heuristics we think should be pinned for perf baselines?

rachel: On it. I'll add --kv-prewarm=30s and a flag --emit-token-histogram.

sam: Will list heuristics and a short doc about when fused vs generic wins. Also add a note: "Don't compare replay vs synth unless kernel path and KV state are matched."

alex: Thanks. If anyone has objections to the experiment matrix, speak up now. Otherwise I'll kick off runs and dump the logs to the perf bucket. :thumbsup:

sam: No objections. +1 to perf bucket.

perf-bot: Created perf bucket folder: gs://redwood-perf/eng-runtime/1835123456-kernel-routing-experiments

alex: Great, I'll post results here when runs finish.

rachel: Quick reminder: when reporting p95/p99, include sample size and whether it's per-request or per-token. Small samples can make p99 meaningless.

alex: noted — will include N, histogram, and KV_hit curves.

sam: Also consider adding a "match-fidelity" label to each run (replay-exact, replay-jittered, synth-matched) so downstream dashboards can filter.

alex: Done — thanks all.
